summary.text: A Mediterranean climate, also called a dry summer climate, is a temperate type with hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters.
It is usually found along the western coasts of landmasses, between roughly 30 and 45 degrees north or south of the equator.
Its dry summers come from the subtropical ridge, which shifts toward the pole in summer and back toward the equator in winter.

facts.label: Köppen code
facts.value: Cs, split into hot Csa and cool Csb

facts.label: Typical latitudes
facts.value: About 30 to 45 degrees north or south

facts.label: Summer dry spell
facts.value: Four to six months without significant rain

items.prompt: A farmer in a Mediterranean climate wants to water her crops with rain alone. Which part of the year will give her almost nothing?

options.label: Winter and early spring
Late autumn only
Summer and early fall
No season; it is even

items.explain: Nearly all precipitation falls in winter and spring, and four to six months of summer and early fall can pass without significant rain.

items.prompt: What keeps summers so dry in places with a Mediterranean climate?

options.label: Mountains that block every wind off the sea
A high-pressure ridge that settles over them
Sea water too warm to form any clouds
Polar air too cold to hold moisture

items.explain: In summer the subtropical ridge moves poleward over these regions, keeping the air very dry with few clouds.

items.prompt: San Francisco has a Mediterranean climate, but its summer highs sit around 21 °C. What keeps it so cool?

options.label: Cold water welling up along the coast
Its high elevation above the sea
Frequent summer rainstorms
Snowmelt from nearby peaks

items.explain: Continuous upwelling of cold subsurface waters along the coast gives San Francisco its cool summers.

items.prompt: Which trio of crops has traditionally grown well in Mediterranean-climate regions?

options.label: Rice, tea and sugarcane
Maize, potatoes and beans
Bananas, coffee and cocoa
Wheat, grapes and olives

items.explain: Wheat, grapes and olives, the "Mediterranean trinity", have traditionally been grown successfully in these areas, hence their wines, oils and breads.

items.prompt: On a summer trip to a Mediterranean-climate region you notice hot afternoons but cool nights. What explains the big swing?

options.label: Sea breezes that blow only after dark
Strong sun by day and fast cooling at night
Summer rain showers that fall every evening
Cold winds sweeping down from the pole

items.explain: Like deserts, these climates have strong solar heating during the day and rapid cooling at night in the warm months.

items.prompt: Funchal and Tashkent both fall under the Mediterranean climate type. How do their winters compare?

options.label: Both are mild and almost frost-free
Both bring snow and frost every year
Tashkent's bring frost and snow; Funchal's don't
Funchal's bring frost and snow; Tashkent's don't

items.explain: Funchal has mild to warm winters where frost and snow are almost unknown, while Tashkent has cold winters with yearly frosts and snowfall.
